chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the marriage of a female slave. He said: 'The marriage of a female slave is not valid except with the permission of her master.'

Sheikh (Al-Tusi) said, may Allah have mercy on him: 'If the master stipulated upon the man in the contract that the child would be enslaved, then the child from her would be a slave to her master. And if he did not stipulate that for him, then the child would be free, and there is no claim of anyone upon him. As for that which indicates that if he did not stipulate, the child would be free, is what he narrated:'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of a female slave and the status of her children according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the conditions for valid marriage with a female slave (amah), emphasizing the necessity of the master's consent. It further details the legal status of offspring, distinguishing between those born into slavery if the master stipulated it in the contract and those born free if no such condition was made, a principle supported by the cited evidence. This ruling reflects the nuanced Shia jurisprudence on manumission and family structure within the context of slavery.
